# Microsoft — Microsoft for Startups

Azure credits for early-stage B2B startups in two paths: a no-referral path starting at $1,000 for 90 days, and an investor-referral path that Microsoft's FAQ says most startups begin at $100,000, with the landing page advertising up to $150,000.

| **Last verified** | 2026-09-14 by [@tayyabakmal1](https://github.com/tayyabakmal1) |
| **Category** | [☁️ Cloud](../categories/cloud.md) |


## What you get

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | credit |
| **Maximum** | $150,000 — see the vendor's exact wording below |
| **Duration** | 24 months |
| **Expiry** | You must activate your Azure credits within 90 days of accepting the Microsoft for Startups program agreement. Once activated, Azure credits provided through Microsoft for Startups are valid for up to two years. Extensions are not available. |
| **When it ends** | Your Azure Sponsorship subscription automatically converts to pay-as-you-go once your Azure credits are fully used or expired, whichever comes first. |

### Tiers

Each tier has its own eligibility. A headline figure is usually the top tier, not
what a typical applicant receives.

| Tier | Amount | The vendor's wording | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Azure startup credit offer (no investor referral code) | $1,000 | If you're new to Azure, you can start with the Azure startup credit offer: $1,000 for 90 days, then an additional $4,000 for 180 days after business verification. | No partner needed |
| Investor offer (10-character referral code required) | $100,000 | The investor offer includes Azure credits (most startups begin with $100,000, with the opportunity to earn more) | A partner code is required |

### Not covered

- Subsidiaries of larger organizations (must be privately held and independent)
- Non-B2B startups
- Accounts with a prior Azure account
- Work, school or company-domain email accounts at signup

> **Stacking:** Credits cannot be transferred to another Microsoft account and are tied to the subscription created at redemption. Benefits generally cannot be redeemed on an account that has previously redeemed the same startup offer, or on an existing enterprise account.

### Notes

VENDOR SELF-CONTRADICTION: the marketing landing page advertises "up to $150,000 in credits" while Microsoft Learn's FAQ states the investor offer means "most startups begin with $100,000, with the opportunity to earn more" and that startups without a referral code get only "$1,000 for 90 days, then an additional $4,000 for 180 days after business verification". The more conservative figures are the Learn ones and are recorded in tiers[]. Could not inspect: the application portal itself - the "Get started now" link resolves to https://portal.azure.com/?homeview=startup#home which returned 403, and https://portal.startups.microsoft.com/ returns a JS-only shell - so tier assignment in-product was not inspectable. Microsoft also states it "doesn't publicly share the list of participating investors", so the partner list is not inspectable. Independently re-audited: a second reviewer opened the vendor page and checked the quote, amount and source.
